gradingSemantic: CURRENT COLLEGE FOOTBALL ABILITY AT RUNNING BACK RIGHT NOW; 2026 is the leading evidence, 2025 is a substantial stabilizer, older evidence is secondary. Grade vision/decision-making, burst, elusiveness, contact balance/power, creation beyond blocking, short-yardage, receiving, ball security and pass-game usefulness. No NFL projection, recruiting ranking, draft stock, fame/school prestige, fantasy value, or future-upside bonus. Injury/availability generally does not directly reduce underlying ability.
currentSeasonWeighting: Middle-ground CFB standard locked by Cody: approximately 55-60% current 2026 performance/role, 30-35% 2025 demonstrated level, remainder older/context; conceptual guidance, not a literal formula.

evidenceSnapshot.note: Evidence is frozen after the September 26-27 weekend so October 3 games in progress do not create inconsistent within-position timing.

resolvedPressurePoints: Hardy remains 92 rather than elite-ceiling range: zero 2026 games matter in college, but injury is not treated as proof his underlying ability disappeared.
Lacy remains 91: current year is quieter, while his dominant 2025 prevents a four-game overcorrection.
Isaac Brown remains 86: excellent prior evidence stabilizes him, but 2026 performance materially lowers him from EA 92.
Duke Clark was corrected from an initial 73 to 86 after the external sanity check exposed elite 2026 efficiency; this is exactly the intended use of the EA/stat audit.
Xavier Brown was corrected down from an initial 87 to 84 because his 2026 return has flashed but the role/sample is too small for the upper-80s.
The bottom remains deliberately separated; curated membership does not imply an 80 floor.

rangeSeparationAudit.note: Secondary backs, thin-sample players and weak Wheel options are allowed into the 70s. No grade was raised merely because the player survived curation.

eaDiscrepancyAudit.source: EA SPORTS College Football 27 current Week 4 HB ratings where an exact current player entry could be resolved
eaDiscrepancyAudit.rule: Absolute HQ-vs-EA difference of 7+ requires mandatory review; 10+ requires explicit major-red-flag explanation. EA is an error detector, never a formula or required midpoint.

mandatoryReviews.explanation: The user-approved 80 anchor intentionally weights 2026 heavily: 107 rushing yards at 2.7 per carry through three games. Prior production prevents a deeper fall, but EA 87 is too reputation-heavy for the current CFB model.
EA 72 materially undersells a back who produced 1,182 rushing yards in 2025. Limited 2026 usage prevents a high grade, but 81 better balances current role with demonstrated recent ability.
Current 2026 production (382 rushing yards at 7.5 per carry through four games) is materially ahead of EA's 78; 87 remains appropriate because the prior RB sample is thin.
Current all-purpose impact is elite: 328 rushing yards, 154 receiving yards and nine total touchdowns through four games. EA's 88 has not caught up to his current level.

postGradeDistribution.note: Distribution was inspected only after player-by-player grading and audits; no grade was moved to manufacture a target shape.

runtimeBoundary: No production/runtime behavior is changed by this artifact. It is calibration authority only for later server-owned Wheel grading integration.
futureVersioning: Any future RB grade change must record previous grade, new grade, effective date, concise reason, and nearby anchor/peer sanity check. Normal maintenance is a targeted exception scan, not a wholesale regrade.
